item.title: Millcreek buildings in 3D
item.snippet: Lidar building roof forms of Millcreek, Utah, shaded by median roof height, standing on the city's 0.5 m lidar terrain. Unvalidated planning estimates; not surveyed or field-verified.
item.description:
Planning estimates. The layers in this scene are unvalidated estimates derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. They have not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use them for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

The 0.5 m lidar bare-earth terrain in the ground (above Esri's World Elevation), 21,561 building models shaded light to darker grey by median roof height, with edges (click one for its heights and flags), and the lidar hillshade draped on the ground. Slides show four parts of the city. The three-way hybrid uses 20,730 roofer LoD2.2 models, 647 Esri LOD2.0 roofs and 184 Esri LOD1.2 blocks. Roof measurements are available only on the retained roofer models.

Place labels are Esri's OpenStreetMap 3D labels (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors).

Trees are not in the scene: the lidar treetops are vector tiles without heights, which can only lie flat on the ground, and OpenStreetMap maps no trees in Millcreek. 3D trees need the lidar treetops as a hosted point layer with their heights.

Lidar source. The 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS project UT_2023SaltLakeCo_C24, USGS 3D Elevation Program), flown on October 7, November 2 and November 4, 2023. Quality level 1 means at least 8 pulses per square metre and a vertical accuracy (RMSEz) of 10 cm or better on open, non-vegetated ground under the USGS specification; the vendor's own accuracy report for this project has not been reviewed for these products. For these products the building and vegetation classes of the points were refined; the ground class was not changed. All products are gridded at 0.5 m.

Coordinates and heights. Built in NAD83(2011) / UTM zone 12N (EPSG 6341), metres, and taken to WGS84 / Web Mercator for ArcGIS Online with the transformation WGS_1984_(ITRF08)_To_NAD_1983_2011. Every layer in the Millcreek LiDAR 2023 set uses this same transformation, so the layers line up with each other and with Esri's basemaps to a few centimetres; without it they would sit about 1.2 m apart. Elevations are NAVD88 (Geoid18) in metres; heights are metres above the lidar bare-earth terrain.

Questions or corrections: City of Millcreek GIS. The processing records (scripts, checks and run logs) are kept by City of Millcreek GIS.

Explore the buildings

Use Search to find an address, choose a slide for a neighborhood, then zoom in and select a building. Drag to rotate the scene; Home returns to the starting view. The legend explains the gray height classes. Daylight changes the illustrative lighting.

What the models show

The three-way hybrid contains 21,561 buildings: 20,730 detailed roofer LoD2.2 models, 647 Esri LOD2.0 roofs and 184 Esri LOD1.2 blocks. Each building uses the selected model for that footprint. Simpler roofs retain city coverage where a detailed roof did not pass the model checks. The pop-up reports the model source and any fallback reason.

Read a building pop-up

Median and upper roof heights describe the lidar points above the local ground. Modelled ridge and eave heights describe the reconstructed roof; they are different measurements. Footprint area is horizontal ground coverage. Roof surface area includes the sloping roof faces, so it can exceed the footprint area. The support percentage reports how much of the footprint contains roof points, not a probability that the model is correct.

Detailed roof measurements are present only for the 20,730 retained roofer models. A blank value on an Esri fallback means unavailable; zero means the model has none of that measured area. Flat roof area uses slopes below 5 degrees; compass-facing areas use slopes from 5 to 70 degrees. Bearings are degrees clockwise from north. Facing areas are screening measurements, not estimates of usable solar area or electricity production. Roof angles remain in degrees.

Downloads and limitations

Building measurements in feet and square feet (CSV) · 3D building package (SLPK) · Full model methods and field definitions

Join the CSV to the models using FP_ID. The SLPK keeps its original metric coordinates and source fields; the CSV provides converted measurements. A detailed-looking roof is still an inferred planning model. Dormers, overhangs, small structures and occluded roof sections can be simplified or incorrect. Lighting and shadows illustrate geometry and are not a validated solar or shadow study.

Dates and units

The source is the 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar, flown in October and November 2023. These maps describe that survey, not present-day conditions. Buildings removed, trees planted or construction completed since then may differ. Basemap imagery can be from a different date.

Height legends and building heights use feet; building areas use square feet. Canopy-zone summaries use acres and percentages. One international foot is exactly 0.3048 meter. The original coordinate system, elevation reference and metric analysis files remain intact so all layers stay aligned. Rounded display values do not imply survey precision.

Questions or corrections: City of Millcreek GIS. Include the map location and building ID when available.
item.licenseInfo:
These data are unvalidated planning estimates produced by City of Millcreek GIS from 2023 lidar. They are not surveyed, engineered or field-verified, and must not be used to determine property boundaries or ownership, building or site design, engineering, flood or drainage design, code compliance (including building height), or any legal or regulatory determination. They are provided as is, without warranty of accuracy, completeness or fitness for any purpose; check conditions on the ground before relying on them. Credit "City of Millcreek GIS; 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (USGS 3DEP)" when you use or show them.

Salt Lake County data. The building footprints and their County attributes come from Salt Lake County (Assessor and Surveyor). The County's own terms apply to them: the County states that its footprints are not field verified, are for general reference only, and are not intended to determine property ownership, final building and site design or jurisdictional boundaries, or to replace a certified topographical or boundary survey or any other legal document.
